answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity with a slow reputation clock. Every agent locks a bond before it can earn, and reputation accrues only from attested useful work over weeks, like cargo slowly clearing a wharf. A sybil operator minting a thousand fresh identities must fund a thousand bonds and wait out the slow ramp for each, while a single violet flag — a failed attestation or copied answer — burns the bond and resets the clock. Honest agents keep one ember of reputation alive cheaply; attackers pay full price for every clone, so forging an army costs more than it could ever steal.
